## COA Measurement Strategy — Multiple Myeloma Phase 3

**In one sentence:** This Phase 3 proteasome inhibitor trial needs to demonstrate superior tolerability and physical function maintenance with PRO endpoints positioned to support secondary labelling claims, given FDA's 2024 precedent favouring MRD as primary efficacy endpoints in RRMM [(Federal Register)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/01/21/2026-01068/minimal-residual-disease-and-complete-response-in-multiple-myeloma-use-as-endpoints-to-support).

**Key challenge:** Balancing comprehensive domain coverage against patient burden in a frail RRMM population while establishing change sensitivity for proteasome inhibitor-specific tolerability advantages.

**Recommended starting point:** EORTC QLQ-C30 + MY20 (change-sensitive, regulatory precedent), MySIm-Q (RRMM-specific validation), and EQ-5D-5L (HTA requirement) — based on KG evidence showing change detection across comparator PI trials [TI-003], [TI-004], [TI-005].

**Critical gap:** EQ-5D-5L essential for NICE/ICER markets but shows variable responsiveness in RRMM — must verify country-specific value sets for global footprint or face HTA submission delays.

## Key Observations

• **PRO endpoint positioning precedent:** In 137 KG trial-instrument records for this indication, 83% were secondary endpoints and 16% exploratory, with no primary PRO endpoints recorded [(Table 4, all instruments)](/search?q=RULE-001). This establishes regulatory expectations for secondary positioning and reinforces the need for careful hierarchy design per [RULE-001].

• **Change sensitivity evidence:** TOURMALINE-MM3 achieved significance (p<0.05) across both EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-MY20 domains [TI-003] — the only KG trial showing systematic PRO change detection [(Table 2, TOURMALINE-MM3 row)](/search?q=change). This trial used comprehensive domain coverage rather than selective subscales, suggesting full instrument administration may be necessary for effect detection in RRMM.

• **MCID establishment gaps:** MySIm-Q MCID data expected March 2026 [(Table 3, MySIm-Q MCID Evidence)](/search?q=PMID%2041824255) — trial timeline must account for threshold availability before database lock to support responder analyses per FDA guidance [(PMC)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11707509/).

• **Regulatory landscape shift:** FDA's January 2026 MRD guidance prioritises MRD-negative complete response as the primary endpoint in RRMM trials [(Federal Register)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/01/21/2026-01068/minimal-residual-disease-and-complete-response-in-multiple-myeloma-use-as-endpoints-to-support), positioning PRO endpoints as supportive evidence for tolerability differentiating claims. 

• **Item library consideration:** KG shows 77 comparator trials used EORTC QLQ-MY20 subscales rather than full instruments [(Table 1, disease-related symptoms footnote)](/search?q=calibrated%20SOA). Expert should evaluate whether calibrated short-form administration reduces burden while maintaining psychometric properties per EORTC guidance.

• **Translation readiness critical path:** MySIm-Q's recent development (2023-2026) requires comprehensive translation programme for global deployment [(Table 5, MySIm-Q row)](/search?q=verify), with 12-18 month lead time potentially impacting study startup timelines if not initiated immediately.

## Comparator Analysis

**bortezomib** — FDA precedent drug — no PRO outcome documented — establishes tolerability baseline for PI class comparison, supporting inclusion of treatment-related AE assessment via MySIm-Q side effect domains [COMP-001].

**carfilzomib** — EMA accepted with EORTC QLQ-C30 (GHS/QoL scale only) — demonstrated known tolerability advantages position this trial to differentiate on cardiovascular/renal AEs through MySIm-Q's comprehensive AE impact assessment [COMP-002].

**ixazomib** — EMA accepted using EORTC QLQ-C30 + MY20 combination — oral dosing convenience established precedent for patient-reported adherence/convenience outcomes, challenging current trial to demonstrate superior tolerability profile through comprehensive PRO battery [COMP-003].

**selinexor** — EMA status not reported — known GI/neurological toxicity profile creates differentiation opportunity for PI tolerability via MySIm-Q symptom burden assessment if current trial drug shows superior AE profile [COMP-004].

**panobinostat** — EMA rejected, monotherapy context — HDAC inhibitor combination requirement absent in current PI trial, potentially supporting simpler dosing/tolerability claims through focused MySIm-Q administration [COMP-005].

**Based on comparator evidence:** EORTC QLQ-C30 + MY20 has the strongest change detection signal in this indication because TOURMALINE-MM3 achieved p<0.05 across comprehensive domain coverage [TI-003], while other comparator trials showed null or partial results using selective subscales [TI-001], [TI-002], [TI-004], [TI-005].

## What the Expert Needs to Decide

1. **Instrument selection strategy:** Choose between comprehensive domain coverage (QLQ-C30 + MY20 + MySIm-Q + EQ-5D-5L = 76 items) versus targeted approach prioritising change-sensitive instruments based on TOURMALINE-MM3 precedent.

2. **MySIm-Q inclusion timing:** Include MySIm-Q despite limited regulatory precedent to capture RRMM-specific content validity, or defer until post-approval studies given MCID availability uncertainty.

3. **Alpha-controlled positioning:** Position TTD for global health status as key secondary within hierarchy after PFS/OS, or designate all PRO endpoints as exploratory to avoid multiplicity constraints.

4. **Assessment schedule alignment:** Integrate PRO collection with PK/safety visits to minimise patient burden while capturing early treatment effect signals per proteasome inhibitor mechanism.

5. **Regional value set strategy:** Implement country-specific EQ-5D-5L value sets at study initiation or defer to analysis phase with appropriate statistical methodology for missing value sets.
